previous_statement: Smoothness of the descended inversion. The scalar action is smooth, free on calU_e, and the N>1 quotient-manifold structure of lem-stage1-quotient-manifold-package is the smooth orbit quotient. Since sigma is smooth, preserves calU_e, and is equivariant for the automorphism c |-> conj(c) of U(1), the representative-independent breve-sigma is smooth in quotient charts (equivalently, p o sigma=breve-sigma o p and local smooth sections of the quotient submersion give smooth local expressions); for N=1 it is the unique smooth self-map of a point.
new_statement: Smoothness of the descended inversion. For N>1, equip breve-calU=calU_e/U(1) with the canonical smooth orbit-quotient structure obtained directly from the smooth free scalar action on the smooth manifold calU_e: the orbit map p is a smooth submersion with smooth local sections. Since sigma is smooth, preserves calU_e, and satisfies sigma(cU)=conj(c)sigma(U), the representative-independent map breve-sigma([U])=[sigma(U)] is smooth. For N=1, breve-calU is a point and breve-sigma is its unique smooth self-map.
